# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later reference)

## Format / meta
- Book 1 = Gutenberg "THE FATAL THREE" by M. E. Braddon, 3 vols (Vol I, Vol II, Vol III). Text is marked up with CHAP headings and "END OF VOL." lines.
- Book 2 = Gutenberg "THE INDISCRETIONS OF A LADY'S MAID" by William Le Queux (ebook 77575). Narrated as diary/memoirs of Mariette Le Bas, French femme-de-chambre. 15 chapters; each has a date header.
- Instructions in the prompt: be extremely concise, sacrifice grammar. (Notes themselves are the deliverable here.)

# BOOK 1: THE FATAL THREE (Braddon)

## Vol I (Clotho; or Spinning the Thread) — Chs I–XIV
- Ch I "We have been so happy": Mr John Fausset (middle-aged, stout, ex-wholesale silk merchant, house of Fausset & Co., St Paul's Churchyard and Lyons; wealthy) and wife Maud (Hon. Maud Donfrey, 3rd dau. of Lord Castle-Connell, Irish peer; 19 at marriage, 9 yrs married; young, fair, fashionable). Daughter Mildred (7, golden hair, doll). Fausset asks Maud to adopt orphan Fay (13–14, his distant relation/ward; heiress; he is sole trustee, she is his ward; mother's identity unstated). Maud reluctant; Mildred pleads "Let the little girl come." House: Upper Parchment Street, Grosvenor Sq end, Park Lane side; country house The Hook (Surrey/Thames, between Chertsey and Windsor).
- Ch II "Fay": Fay arrives with Fausset from Streatham Common. Thin, tall, dark, olive complexion, great black eyes, proud, badly dressed. Mildred and Fay bond instantly; "I'll give you my very best doll." Maud gives Fay Bell's room (servant's room, back, mews view). Maud jealous; Fausset insists on inspecting room.
- Ch III "A Superior Person": Mildred loves Fay; Maud jealous/cold. Martha Bell (48, Maud's old nurse, ex-wet-nurse at Castle-Connell, husband Patrick Bell head gardener, emigrated to Canada, died there) rules household, hates Fay; Bell says Fay's linen neglected, "heiress" a fiction. Miss Colville = morning governess.
- Ch IV "All she could remember": Fay's past: childhood cottage on windy hill, sea view, nurse "Nounou", a column with statue; old lady (Brussels school) taught her; she was sent to Brussels finishing... actually earlier English boarding school run by Miss Constable (Miss Constable disliked Fay: "tabula rasa"). At The Hook: Mildred ill with scarlet fever (scarlatina); Fay nurses her. Bell, Meta (Mildred's German maid) gossip overheard by Mildred: Fay is sister. Mildred tells Maud "Why mayn't I call Fay sister?" Maud furious; Fay: "I hate everybody else in this house." Maud: "wicked ungrateful girl." Fausset: "She was once near and dear to me." Mildred sent to Eastbourne with Bell; Fay sent to finishing school in Brussels. Mildred told by letter "Fay dreadfully backward...no manners."
- Ch V "Without the Wolf": Years later, 1870s-era (setting: George and Mildred Greswold, Enderby Manor, near Romsey, Hampshire). Mildred Fausset m. George Greswold (formerly George Ransome; married "fourteen years" by Ch VIII-ish; actually married 13 years at Lola's death). Daughter Lola (Laura), 12, golden hair, blue eyes. Fever in village (typhoid); cause: polluted well used for dairy (Mrs Wadman, dairy-woman; her husband the cowkeeper; bailiff Thomas; sister from Salisbury had typhoid). Dr Porter (village doctor, elderly, burly). Dr Hutchinson of Southampton. Lola took beef-tea, milk. Nanny-maid Bell (white-haired Mrs Bell, age 74; Lola's grandmother's nurse). Dog Puck. Greswold: "Red Riding Hood without the wolf." Little Polly Rainbow (flaxen-haired, fair child, dairy pitcher girl, widow Mrs Rainbow's only child) dies. Johnny Giles, Mrs Peter, Janet Dawson, Andrew Rogers, Mary Rainbow, Joe Stanning ill.
- Ch VI "Ah! Pity! The lily is withered": Lola (Laura) dies after fever ("bell that tolled for the widow's only child tolled ten days later for Lola"). Greswold had "one dark memory" (his first marriage). Greswold dismissed Mrs Wadman, bailiff Thomas Wadman / John Thomas (bailiff), housekeeper; "clean sweep" except Bell. Lola's grave: white marble cross, "Laura, the only child of George and Mildred Greswold, aged twelve." Greswold cries "Judgment!" at grave.
- Ch VII "Drifting apart": Greswolds at Lake of Thun villa, then Vienna. Mildred recalls Fay's mother's facts: Fausset's natural daughter. Mrs Fausset (Maud) dies (heart disease) when Mildred 16; deathbed reveals Fay is father's natural daughter by a woman he loved before marrying Maud. Mildred promised to avoid Fay. Mildred's father John Fausset dies in London (inflammation of lungs) in Parchment Street; Mildred ~ 25-ish at death? (aged-consistent). Fausset Bell.
- Ch VIII "Such things were": George Ransome (second son; mother's estate Enderby; assumed name Greswold; Oxford friend of Fausset's father; met Mildred at The Hook, 13 years older; Eton & Oxford). Father Squire Ransome of Mapledown (Sussex), elder brother Randolph. Mother left Enderby to George. Greswold met Mildred 13+ years before; married. Mildred's Lola's grave visit: Greswold cries "Judgment! judgment!"
- Ch IX "The face in the church": Two months later, July. Greswold's dog Kassandra (Irish setter). Niece Pamela Ransome (daughter of Randolph Ransome; sister Rosalind m. Sir Henry Mountford of Rainham Hall; yacht Gadfly; fox-terrier Box). Mildred sees stranger "Judas face" in Enderby Church: red-brown beard/hair, Castellani.
- Ch X "There is always the skeleton": Castellani (César Castellani, Milanese, son of composer; grandfather in silk trade with Fausset/Felix firm, Lyons; author of anonymous novel "Nepenthe"). Guests of Riverdale (Mr Tom Hillersdon, Mrs Louise Hillersdon, formerly Louise Lorraine, ex-courtesan, now pious). Castellani at Enderby reveals Greswold's previous marriage in Nice (Lady Lochinvar's palace). Mildred faints? (No—Ch XI, she is pale; Greswold's dog licks his face.)
- Ch XI "The beginning of doubt": Greswold: first marriage was a secret; he didn't tell. Pamela visits. Castellani.
- Ch XII "She cannot be unworthy": Castellani visits; Mr Cancellor (Clement Cancellor, Vicar of St Elizabeth's, Parchment Street, Mildred's old teacher) to visit Riverdale. Castellani plays Don Giovanni etc. Concert arranged.
- Ch XIII "Shall she be less than another?": Cancellor's history: Louise Hillersdon's repentance. Debate: Deceased Wife's Sister's Bill. Greswold argues marriage with a deceased wife's sister; Cancellor opposes. Greswold: "Rachel" argument.
- Ch XIV "Lifting the curtain": Concert at Enderby. Castellani: "Her death was infinitely sad." Greswold shows Mildred his first wife's photograph; Mildred faints at his feet. Vol I ends.

## Vol II (Lachesis; or the Meter of Destiny) — Chs I–IX
- Ch I "A wife and no wife": Castellani's background (Magnus Dudley, society poet, rumours). Mildred leaves Enderby for Ivy Cottage/Romsey Station; Greswold missed her at station. Letter from Mildred: first wife was Fay (her sister); she goes to Mrs Tomkison in Queen Anne's Gate.
- Ch II "The sins of the fathers": Greswold interviews Bell re Fay; Bell's suspicions. Greswold's first wife Vivien Faux (met at Florence 19 yrs before, English heiress, £30,000, trustee lawyer in Lincoln's Inn; married her before British Consul, Florence).
- Ch III "The verdict of her church": Mildred at Mrs Tomkison (Cecilia, husband Adam). Mildred to Cancellor; Cancellor: "a wife and no wife"; Mildred leaves for Brighton (Miss Gertrude Fausset, aunt, Lewes Crescent).
- Ch IV "No light": Aunt Gertrude Fausset (57, Brighton, Franz the butler). Aunt says Fay died abroad, won't help. Castellani calls on aunt; aunt's secret music ties to Castellani.
- Ch V "The future might be darker": Greswold to Pergament & Pergament (lawyers, Lincoln's Inn Fields) re Vivien; firm won't reveal. Pamela & Box go with him. Mildred's sister-claim; Greswold "Good-bye".
- Ch VI "Higher views": Mildred ill (low fever). Pamela & Castellani flirt. Maltravers (Samuel Maltravers, Vicar of St Edmund's, Brighton) wants Mildred for a transept. Aunt says "Let her marry Castellani." Plan: Pallanza, Lake Maggiore.
- Ch VII "The time has come": Pallanza. Castellani pursues Mildred; she rejects him and dismisses him. Castellani: "a murderer and a madman." Greswold accused by Castellani of murdering first wife (Vivien) at Nice.
- Ch VIII "Not proven": Mildred to Nice. Lady Lochinvar (Hibernian, Palais Montano). Vivien died at Nice by fall from cliff near St Jean. Greswold (then George Ransome) jailed, then asylum at St André (Dr Leroy). Villa "Le Bout du Monde", St Jean. Verdict "not proven."
- Ch IX "Looking back": Mildred visits Villa (renamed Montfleuri), grave. Visits Dr Leroy and asylum; singer Maria Castellani (aunt/cousin of Paolo Castellani; Paolo = César's father; original singer). Verdict: Mildred resolves to go home.

## Vol III (Atropos; or That Which Must Be) — Chs I–XI
- Ch I "A wrecked life": Mildred at Nice; visits Dr Leroy's madhouse; Maria Castellani. Pamela and Stuart (Malcolm Stuart, Scottish soldier, heir to Lady Lochinvar).
- Ch II "In the morning of life": Greswold's backstory: young George Ransome, Greece, Florence; meets Vivien Faux at Signora Vicenti's party; she wanted to be "tolerated/not pitied"; marries him. Her jealousy. Nice, St Jean villa.
- Ch III "The rift in the lute": Vivien jealous of Delia Darcy (Irish girl); Greswold denies; quarrel; Vivien threatens; "Say that you wish me dead." Vivien throws herself over cliff on path near Beaulieu.
- Ch IV "Darkness": Greswold rescued; tried at Villefranche, imprisoned, then asylum (madness). Later mother's death (Squire Ransome? Mother Ransome) and inheritance.
- Ch V "The grave on the hill": Mildred at Nice; Stuart and Pamela; Vivien's grave at Villefranche cemetery "VIVIEN RANSOME, Died April 24th, 1868"; Mildred plants roses.
- Ch VI "Pamela changes her mind": Castellani at Nice; Lady Lochinvar; Malcolm Stuart courting Pamela. Mildred's letter from Brighton/Miss Fausset ill; Mildred to Brighton.
- Ch VII "As the sands run down": Miss Fausset ill; Mildred told. Mildred writes Rollinson (curate, Enderby); reply: Greswold broken-hearted, visits Lola's grave at dusk.
- Ch VIII "How should I greet thee?": Mildred at Enderby churchyard; Greswold cold. Rollinson's lodging. Mildred to Brighton, Miss Fausset's coldness. Pamela's wedding planned at Westminster Abbey; honeymoon at The Hook.
- Ch IX "Litera scripta manet": Mildred at The Hook; finds packet of letters in father's bookcase cupboard (letters from Miss Fausset (Gertrude) as Vivien Faux's mother; Fay = daughter of Gertrude and Paolo Castellani, illegitimate; Gertrude married Castellani in sham civil marriage; John Fausset adopted Fay, "Fanny"; settled 30,000 l. to Fay). So Fay was Gertrude's daughter, NOT Fausset's; Mildred had no sister; Mildred writes curt letter to aunt, returns to Enderby.
- Ch X "Marked by fate": Mildred back at Enderby; reconciliation with Greswold; Mildred's heart weak; physician advises rest. Greswold's despair.
- Ch XI "Like a tale that is told": Pamela married Stuart at Westminster Abbey. Miss Fausset (aunt) confesses to Mildred: Castellani's father (Paolo) seduced her, sham marriage; Fay her daughter; she refused to acknowledge. Aunt dies early winter; Mildred inherits; Greswold lives; Greswold Hospital founded in South London. Castellani later faded from fashion. END OF VOL III / THE END.

**Key names (Book 1):** Mildred (Fausset/Greswold), John Fausset, Maud (Mrs Fausset, née Donfrey), Fay (Vivien Faux / Fanny), Martha Bell, Miss Colville, Miss Constable, Meta, Lola (Laura), George Greswold/Ransome, Vivien Faux, César Castellani, Paolo Castellani, Maria Castellani, Gertrude Fausset (aunt), Clement Cancellor, Louise Hillersdon / Tom Hillersdon, Pamela Ransome, Rosalind, Sir Henry Mountford, Malcolm Stuart, Lady Lochinvar, Rollinson, Maltravers, Dr Porter, Dr Leroy, Mrs Tomkison (Cecilia, Adam), Kassandra, Box, Polly Rainbow, Mrs Rainbow, Mrs Wadman, Lola's dog Puck, Franz, Albrecht.

# BOOK 2: THE INDISCRETIONS OF A LADY'S MAID (Le Queux)
Narrator: Mariette Le Bas, 24, from Pont-Pagny near Auxerre (Yonne), daughter of Jacques Le Bas; femme-de-chambre; wages £48/yr; speaks French, Italian, English, some German. Narrates many mistresses; often overhears keyholes; "Keep a still tongue" theme.

## Ch I Madame's Gentleman Friend (dated April 10)
- Mrs Lucy Engleheart (Cleveland Square, London); husband Monsieur Engleheart (City). Butler Francis (dyed moustache, "Mr Jennings" alias, ex-servant, actually involved). Monte Carlo (Hôtel de Paris). Madame's lover Oswald B. Ogden (American, leather-cornering father, engaged to Gloria Dominick, daughter of Charles H. Dominick, Philadelphia Railway). Madame & Engleheart blackmail scheme with letters; Ogden refuses to pay, threatens police; both vanish from Bayswater; Mariette's wages lost.
- Connection: Vernon (Francis's alias) in Nice Hôtel Royal.

## Ch II The Wardrobe Drawer (dated Oct 9)
- Lady Allardyce (Branksome Court, Bournemouth); husband Sir Hubert Allardyce (ex-Diplomat, South American minister). Lady gives Mariette clothes; locked wardrobe drawer with false bottom holds jewels, revolver, velvet loup, burglary tools. Lover "Charles Shaw" = George Gamlen, jewel thief; arrested in the house by police. Lady claims Shaw is her son. Gamlen later sent to Devil's Island.

## Ch III Little Mrs Otway (dated June 23)
- Mrs Lucy Otway (Grosvenor Street; husband Jack/Monsieur Otway, newspaper proprietor, "Otway's journal"). Lover Hon. Frank Carew (Foreign Office). Financier Isaac Blumfeld (Park Lane) shot dead in library by Madame (Lucy) in struggle over secret treaty papers he was blackmailing with. Carew admits he sold copy to Blumfeld. Mariette paid £100, dismissed.

## Ch IV The Noah's Ark (dated Feb 16)
- Mrs Ashley-Bond (Savoy Hotel; Monsieur Ashley-Bond = Captain Hugh Atherton alias). Friend Madame Courtenay (husband Courtenay). Forgers of £10 Bank of England notes; travel Milan, Palermo (Villa Igiea), Rimini, Messina; Mariette carries child's tin Noah's Ark (hiding 170,000 francs) to Genoa to Courtenay. Agent Pégard (French police; Mariette arrested Marseilles). Courtenay sentenced 15 yrs forced labour, Seine assize.

## Ch V Guilty Bonds (dated July 29)
- Mrs Alleyne (Hembury Court, near Totnes, Devon); husband Monsieur Alleyne (Philip). Chauffeur Chapman; Jack (chauffeur/footman). Major Hubert Ward (jealous, ex-Cape Town card-sharper, shot by Alleyne in night when he robbed safe; real name ended in Mrs Alleyne's first husband). Madame's real first husband = Major Ward ("Ethel" = Madame's name in letters; Ward earlier "Cape Town"); tiara of wheat-ears diamond. Alleyne sold Hembury; moved to Florence.

## Ch VI The Mystery of Monsieur (dated Jan 15)
- Mrs Henniker (Ralph Henniker, alias Farmer/Mortimer; Stamford, Lincolnshire). Butler Gray (blackmailer). Jean Valensi (French police agent, waiter at "The George"). Murder at Norfolk Square of George Bicknell by Mrs Henniker (Lucy). Mariette drugged with cocaine coffee; rescued. Lucy 20 years penal servitude; Gray in Marseilles prison.

## Ch VII The Chamber of Secrets (dated July 2)
- 18 April 1909 Florence. Chief of police Luigi Ansaldi. William Cornforth (Guglielmo, Villa Borelli, Florence; steel strong-room). Mistress Madame Kennedy-Foster (Villa Luba, Viale; a devout widow, her "Madame"). Cornforth shot in strong room; agent Enrico Ferri's report of old woman visiting at night. Mariette dismissed.

## Ch VIII What was in the strong room (dated July 28)
- Hidden cavity behind picture: unset gems (diamonds, rubies, emeralds). Second murder: detective Carlo Bruno shot in strong room. Scotland Yard (Commissioner Chetwynd) told Italian police to hush up. British Consul Monsieur Walker. Inspector Stephens (Scotland Yard) explains Cornforth criminal "most dangerous". Cornforth's Brighton house (Brunswick Square, Hove).

## Ch IX Concerns Two Visitors (dated Sept 2)
- Karl Flugel (old German, grey eyes, spectacles, blue reefer jacket) and Miss Agnes Cornforth (Cornforth's daughter, believed drowned at Sheringham/Hunstanton 18 months before). Flugel knows truth; wants to profit from secret; Agnes lives in village 3 miles from York.

## Ch X Contains Some Revelations (dated Dec 22)
- Dec: Flugel found dead in strong room (shot by invisible ray); Agnes arrested. Cornforth = Hertzian-ray electric weapon inventor; wife Madame Kennedy-Foster (Mrs Cornforth) disguised as old woman. Destructive apparatus; secret lost (broken) in strong room. Agnes returns to mother in Brussels.

## Ch XI A Queer Ménage (dated Sept 6)
- Mr & Mrs Shorland (Albert Hall Mansions, Kensington Gore; Madame's father Mr March, invalid, Allandale, Oakleigh Park). American millionaires Lindermann (John R. Lindermann, Pittsburg; Ida, wife; agent Lamb). Chateau de Bouligny, Marlotte, Fontainebleau. Marie Antoinette's emerald crucifix stolen from Louvre. Shorlands fled; Mariette paid by March.

## Ch XII A Peer of the Realm (dated April 5)
- Lady Lydgate ("Angel"; husband Earl of Lydgate, "Tubby", Hubert; 17th Earl). Butler Thompson (48 yrs service; hated her). Captain Fletcher her lover. Earl shot in Berkshire accident; dies. Lady left for Paris with Fletcher; note from her.

## Ch XIII Concerning Madame's Luggage (dated Aug 29)
- Madame Houget (Provençal; husband Pierre Houget, Lyons manufacturer); Princess di Lastra a Signa (Maria), daughters Claudia and Vittorina; Villa at Vallombrosa; sapphires of Sultan Suleyman. Madame's trick: Jean Regnier (baggage porter) plants jewels in her trunk; at Pisa Madame feigns illness; sells to Jacobsen in Amsterdam; Mariette given 1,000 francs.

## Ch XIV Madame and the Butler (dated Feb 17)
- Mrs Wentworth (Elmhurst Court, Sussex; Captain Wentworth, weak heart; daughter Doris; governess Miss Wylde; earlier French governess Lucie Perrin; butler Charles Ford (killer of Perrin, ran illicit Hamburg gaming house); insect-puncture marks; diphtheria; plot with culture tube from Gervais (Earl's Court Road); Mariette exposes Ford at dinner ice pudding; Madame pays Mariette £100.

## Ch XV The People at Lancaster Gate (dated June 11)
- Miss Violet Rutherford-Morgan and father (really Dick Traill & Lily Mayhew, Shorland gang jewel thieves; chauffeur Edwards; Mr Cave accomplice). Fake diamond necklace purchase from Horton Brothers, Old Bond Street. Mariette arrested, released. Mariette returns to Pont-Pagny, saved a few thousand francs. END.
